== Biography ==
'''Margaret C. Glasgow''' was born on '''May 3, 1820''', in '''Washington County, Pennsylvania'''. She was the daughter of '''James Glasgow''' and '''Betsey A. (Sleator) Glasgow''', both of whom were natives of '''Ireland'''.

In '''1832''', when Margaret was twelve years old, the Glasgow family moved from Pennsylvania to '''Ohio''' by team, initially settling in '''Knox County'''. The following year, in '''1833''', they relocated to '''Richland County''', Ohio. The family faced challenges during these early years, such as a severe frost in '''June 1834''' that caused significant damage to the crops. 

Margaret's father, '''James Glasgow''', purchased '''eighty acres of land''' where Joseph Hainley would later reside, and the family lived in a '''log cabin'''. James Glasgow continued farming there for several years before spending his final days in '''Henry County, Ohio'''.

Margaret was raised in a pioneering environment and witnessed the growth and development of her family's farm in Richland County. Her siblings and extended family became an integral part of their Ohio community.

She lived through a period of rapid growth and change in the region and was part of a family that contributed significantly to the local farming community.

Published in 1901
Source: Internet Archive

On the 2d of May, 1844. Mr. Ferguson was united in marriage to Miss
Margaret C. Glasgow, who was born in Washington county, Pennsylvania,
May 3. 1820. a daughter of James and Betsy A. (Sleator) Glasgow, both
natives of Ireland. Her family removed from Pennsylvania to Ohio by team in
1832, and first settled in Knox county, but a year later came to Richland county.
In June. 1834. there was a heavy frost, which did much damage to the crops.
Mr. Glasgow purchased eighty acres of land where Joseph Hainley now re-
sides, and erected thereon a log cabin. Here he followed farming for some
years, but his last days were spent in Henry county.
